bundle.text:
# The dsh-tui bundle patch: the interactive terminal front door over the
# dsh-base layer. Applied after dsh-base's insert; rows here override base
# rows by id, with the profile's own cordis.patch.yml and any --patch
# overlays still to come.
#
# A patch replaces the targeted row's whole `config`, so each row below
# restates every key it owns (see the dsh-base patch for the shared
# defaults). The dsh-base core rows that need no dsh-tui value — tools,
# sandbox/approval policy, skills, goal, plan mode, workspace context,
# telemetry — are inherited unchanged.

# ── surface-specific values over the dsh-base layer ─────────────────────────

# The dsh-tui deployment persona; DSH_TUI_PERSONA overrides the coding-agent
# default (the base persona is empty). dsh-system-prompt renamed the slot at
# 0.1.3-alpha.2 (`persona` → `personaPrefix`, with an optional suffix
# counterpart); older cohorts only accept `persona`, so the key follows the
# installed package version.
- id: system-prompt
  config: !!js >-
    (() => {
      const persona = process.env.DSH_TUI_PERSONA ?? 'You are a coding agent.'
      try {
        const require = process.getBuiltinModule('node:module').createRequire(ctx.baseUrl)
        const fs = process.getBuiltinModule('node:fs')
        const manifest = require.resolve('@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt/package.json')
        const version = String(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(manifest, 'utf8')).version ?? '')
        const match = /^(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)/u.exec(version)
        const [major, minor, patch] = match === null ? [0, 0, 0] : [Number(match[1]), Number(match[2]), Number(match[3])]
        if (major > 0 || minor > 1 || (minor === 1 && patch >= 3)) return { personaPrefix: persona }
        return { persona }
      } catch {
        return { personaPrefix: persona }
      }
    })()

# The native DeepSeek adapter, pinned to the harness defaults: full thinking
# at max effort, key and base URL from the launching environment. The base
# entry supplies the adapter defaults; /settings edits the profile config
# on 0.1.7 (older hosts apply their separate settings document per request).
# rc.6 schema key is `apiKeyEnv` (credential-ref env var NAME, default
# DEEPSEEK_API_KEY); the old snapshot's `apiKey` key no longer exists.
- id: llm-deepseek
  config:
    apiKeyEnv: 'DEEPSEEK_API_KEY'
    baseURL: !!js process.env.DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL
    thinking: enabled
    reasoningEffort: max

# The TUI creates (or resumes) its agent at runtime through the agent
# factory; no declarative agents are started at boot, and the configured
# agent list stays the base's empty default.
- id: agent-loop
  config:
    agents: []

# ── agent presets (issue #8) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The model-facing plugin set moves INTO the preset registry: every
# session composes its tools/prompt sections from one preset
# (standard/ptc/minimal/cordis) instead of the host rows below. The TUI's
# roster row uses the scoped `dsh-tui-agent-presets` id. The 0.1.2 generation
# prepends its bundled system root; legacy 0.1.1-rc.2 still needs the dsh CLI's
# `config/agent-presets/` directory supplied explicitly. Both append
# `$DSH_HOME/.agent-presets`. Mirroring the official dsh-web-app patch: every
# dsh-base row a preset now owns is disabled here, so a minimal agent does not
# leak host-layer tools (an agent's registry view resolves agent → preset →
# global). On 0.1.7, the adapter registers official declarative bundles;
# directory discovery and the old code-runtime host row stay disabled.

- id: agent-instructions
  disabled: true

- id: command-compact
  disabled: true

# compaction lives in the preset's own isolate realm (standard/ptc/cordis
# carry `compaction-basic` with package defaults; minimal has none). The old
# ratio/retain tunables retired with this host row — preset compositions own
# their compaction config.
- id: compaction-basic
  disabled: true

- id: plan-mode
  disabled: true

- id: skill-filesystem
  disabled: true

- id: tool-bash
  disabled: true

- id: tool-fs
  disabled: true

- id: tool-fs-search
  disabled: true

- id: command-goal
  # rc.2 presets do not carry this command, so their host row must remain
  # active. Newer packages disable it only when the shipped standard preset
  # really owns the command; reading the capability avoids guessing from
  # another optional Loader row.
  disabled: !!js >-
    (() => {
      const require = process.getBuiltinModule('node:module').createRequire(ctx.baseUrl)
      const fs = process.getBuiltinModule('node:fs')
      const path = process.getBuiltinModule('node:path')
      try {
        require.resolve('@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry/package.json')
        return true
      } catch {}
      try {
        const manifest = require.resolve('@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets/package.json')
        const preset = path.join(path.dirname(manifest), 'presets', 'standard', 'agent.cordis.yml')
        return fs.readFileSync(preset, 'utf8')
          .split(/\r?\n/u)
          .some(line => line.trim() === '- id: command-goal')
      } catch {
        return false
      }
    })()

- id: tool-goal
  disabled: true

- id: tool-jobs
  disabled: true

- id: tool-pwsh
  disabled: true

- id: tool-ralph
  disabled: true

- id: tool-result-pruner
  disabled: true

- id: tool-skill
  disabled: true

# `tool-str-replace-editor` carries no disable row: dsh-base registered that
# entry only up to the 0.1.2 line, and from 0.1.3-alpha.2 it is opt-in (see the
# dsh-base README). A row here would target a missing id and log
# `patch: entry "tool-str-replace-editor" not found` on every 0.1.3+ boot.
# Presets that expose the tool re-add the entry themselves.

# Delegation tools (subagent spawn/fork, controls, workflows) are preset rows
# now; the preset's `delegation` group re-adds them with package defaults, so
# the former TUI's depth-1 cap no longer applies.
- id: tool-subagent
  disabled: true

- id: tool-subagent-control
  disabled: true

- id: tool-subagent-fork
  disabled: true

- id: tool-subagent-list-agents
  disabled: true

- id: tool-todo
  disabled: true

- id: tool-web
  disabled: true

- id: tool-workflow
  disabled: true

# Windows has no sandbox confinement backend yet (sandbox-local's win32
# chain is empty); use danger-full-access on Windows so bash commands can
# run. Other platforms keep the base workspace-write default. DSH_PERMISSION_MODE
# is the INITIAL state of a launch — the remembered /permission pick
# (~/.dsh-tui/permission.json) outranks it whenever it is not set.
- id: sandbox-policy
  config:
    mode: !!js "process.platform === 'win32' ? 'danger-full-access' : (process.env.DSH_PERMISSION_MODE ?? 'workspace-write')"
    workspaceRoot: !!js process.cwd()

# On Windows, skip approval prompts (no sandbox = the user's terminal trust
# model, matching every other terminal coding agent).
- id: approval
  config:
    policy: !!js "process.platform === 'win32' ? 'never' : ((process.env.DSH_PERMISSION_MODE ?? 'workspace-write') === 'danger-full-access' ? 'never' : 'ask')"

# Sessions live in the shared JSONL store (~/.dsh/sessions) — the same
# backend dsh web writes — so /resume here and the web session list see each
# other (#24). The row itself comes from the dsh-base layer; this override
# only re-points the root when DSH_TUI_SESSION_ROOT is set (test isolation).
- id: session-persistence-jsonl
  config:
    root: !!js process.env.DSH_TUI_SESSION_ROOT ?? dshHomePath('sessions')

# ── dsh-tui rows ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# The `user-interaction` service row comes from the dsh-base bundle layer
# (mounted before this layer); do not insert it again — the include patch
# semantics would create a duplicate row. dsh-tui defensively creates the
# service on its own context when no composition provides it (bare
# `dsh --config cordis.yml` boots), then mounts the model-facing
# ask_user_question tool. On legacy hosts it registers the TUI provider on
# `ctx.userQuestions`; on Alpha it answers the scoped
# `user-questions/request` waterfall.

- insert:
    # Workspace grouping is a separate durable ledger, not a cwd-derived
    # projection. Mount the same domain stack and storage root as dsh-web-app
    # so TUI-created sessions can attach to the exact registry Web reads.
    #
    # These rows own host-plane services that the official web-app bundle may
    # already mount. Loader entry ids are process-global, so these
    # rows use dsh-tui-* scoped ids and self-disable when an enabled row with
    # the official id/name is already present in the tree. The disabled check
    # is evaluated during the same include update that inserts every row, so
    # it sees the web-app rows regardless of their activation state.
    - id: dsh-tui-storage
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage'
      disabled: !!js "[...ctx.loader.entries()].some(entry => entry.options.id === 'storage' && entry.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage' && !entry.disabled)"

    - id: dsh-tui-storage-json
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-json'
      disabled: !!js "[...ctx.loader.entries()].some(entry => entry.options.id === 'storage-json' && entry.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-json' && !entry.disabled)"
      config:
        root: !!js dshHomePath('storages')

    - id: dsh-tui-storage-domain
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-domain'
      disabled: !!js "[...ctx.loader.entries()].some(entry => entry.options.id === 'storage-domain' && entry.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-domain' && !entry.disabled)"
      config:
        backend: json

    # Alpha moved the durable storage stack into dsh-base, so these three
    # scoped copies self-disable there. Keep them for the validated rc lines,
    # whose base layer does not provide the stack to a TUI-only profile.

    - id: dsh-tui-workspace
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workspace'
      disabled: !!js "[...ctx.loader.entries()].some(entry => entry.options.id === 'workspace' && entry.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workspace' && !entry.disabled)"

    # PTC presentation waits on this Host service. The scoped row supports a
    # TUI-only profile and yields to the official web-app row in mixed profiles.
    - id: dsh-tui-code-runtime
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-code-runtime-worker-thread'
      disabled: !!js >-
        (() => {
          const require = process.getBuiltinModule('node:module').createRequire(ctx.baseUrl)
          try { require.resolve('@deepseek-ai/dsh-ptc-runtime-node/package.json'); return true } catch {}
          return [...ctx.loader.entries()].some(entry => entry.options.id === 'code-runtime' && entry.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-code-runtime-worker-thread' && !entry.disabled)
        })()

    # 0.1.2 presets opt their delegation tool into Host-owned model-selection
    # settings. Without this service standard/ptc/cordis preset mounting fails.
    # The package subpath does not exist on rc.2, so resolve that capability
    # directly before Loader attempts the import. An enabled official row still
    # owns the seat in mixed profiles.
    - id: dsh-tui-subagent-model-selection-settings
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent/model-selection-settings'
      disabled: !!js >-
        (() => {
          const require = process.getBuiltinModule('node:module').createRequire(ctx.baseUrl)
          try {
            require.resolve('@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent/model-selection-settings')
          } catch {
            return true
          }
          return [...ctx.loader.entries()].some(entry => entry.options.id === 'subagent-model-selection-settings' && entry.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent/model-selection-settings' && !entry.disabled)
        })()

    # Generic terminal workspace registry. Optional plugins add providers;
    # the TUI itself always supplies LOCAL and has no provider-specific code.
    - id: dsh-tui-workspaces
      name: '@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui/workspaces'

    # Optional plugins contribute nested slash-command completion here;
    # execution and durable command events remain owned by dsh-commands.
    - id: dsh-tui-command-trees
      name: '@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui/command-trees'
    # Optional plugins declare editable settings sections here (issue #165);
    # storage, validation and writes remain owned by the dsh settings service.
    - id: dsh-tui-settings-sections
      name: '@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui/settings-sections'

    # Optional plugins register full-screen scenes (trajectory-style whole-
    # terminal views) here and open them from their own command handlers;
    # rendering and input ownership remain owned by the TUI's Chat screen.
    - id: dsh-tui-scenes
      name: '@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui/scenes'

    # Optional plugins register side-panel surfaces (sidebar Panel +
    # compact row, experimental §18) here; admission, budgets and crash
    # isolation remain owned by the tuiPanels runtime + PanelStore.
    - id: dsh-tui-panels
      name: '@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui/panels'

    # Plugin-interop anchor (Community Consensus v0.15): the unified grant
    # store, runtime generation id, and Host Descriptor live here; later
    # contract surfaces (plugin storage, message observation, effect
    # ledger) mount off THIS row's apply, so the patch surface changes only
    # once for the whole alignment. Mounted ahead of the extensions row and
    # any third-party plugin row.
    - id: dsh-tui-plugin-host
      name: '@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui/plugin-host'

    # Plugin-facing UI seams (the pi-style extension surface): managed
    # dialogs (select/confirm/input), keyed status-line contributions,
    # keyboard shortcuts, and custom session-entry text renderers. The
    # decision events (tui/input, tui/rewind-prompt, tui/session-switch,
    # tui/compact, …) are fired by the channel on the cordis bus directly
    # and need no row.
    - id: dsh-tui-extensions
      name: '@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui/extensions'

    # The agent-preset roster (issue #8): `ctx.agentPresets`, the service the
    # TUI composes every session's model-facing world from. 0.1.2 packages
    # prepend their bundled presets as the read-only system root; legacy rc.2
    # packages have no bundled root and still scan the dsh CLI directory. Both append
    # `$DSH_HOME/.agent-presets` as the user root. Deployment-added roots may
    # still be supplied by a later patch.
    - id: dsh-tui-agent-presets
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets'
      disabled: !!js >-
        (() => {
          const require = process.getBuiltinModule('node:module').createRequire(ctx.baseUrl)
          try { require.resolve('@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry/package.json'); return true } catch {}
          return [...ctx.loader.entries()].some(entry => entry.options.id === 'agent-presets' && entry.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets' && !entry.disabled)
        })()
      config: !!js >-
        (() => {
          const require = process.getBuiltinModule('node:module').createRequire(ctx.baseUrl)
          const fs = process.getBuiltinModule('node:fs')
          const path = process.getBuiltinModule('node:path')
          try {
            const manifest = require.resolve('@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets/package.json')
            if (fs.existsSync(path.join(path.dirname(manifest), 'presets'))) {
              return { default: 'standard' }
            }
          } catch {
            // Let the roster import report a missing package; preserve the rc
            // root fallback below for every package generation without one.
          }
          const base = ctx.baseUrl
          if (!base) return { default: 'standard' }
          const root = new URL('../node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/config/agent-presets/', base)
          let rootPath = decodeURIComponent(root.pathname)
          if (/^\/[A-Za-z]:/.test(rootPath)) rootPath = rootPath.slice(1)
          return { default: 'standard', roots: [{ path: rootPath, trust: 'system' }] }
        })()

    # 0.1.7 replaces directory discovery with declarations in a registry.
    # The TUI registers the official bundle defaults only when Web has not
    # already declared them. PTC's host runtime now comes from dsh-base.
    - id: dsh-tui-agent-preset-registry
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry'
      disabled: !!js >-
        (() => {
          const require = process.getBuiltinModule('node:module').createRequire(ctx.baseUrl)
          try { require.resolve('@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry/package.json') } catch { return true }
          return [...ctx.loader.entries()].some(entry => entry.options.id === 'agent-preset-registry' && entry.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry' && !entry.disabled)
        })()
      config:
        default: standard

    # Host-plane services the `cordis` preset's plugin-experimentation tool
    # waits on (dynamicCordisRunner/cordisInspect); dsh-base carries no such
    # row — the official web app inserts it the same way, so this copy yields
    # to it when it is already present.
    - id: dsh-tui-cordis-host-runner
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-cordis-host-runner'
      disabled: !!js "[...ctx.loader.entries()].some(entry => entry.options.id === 'cordis-host-runner' && entry.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-cordis-host-runner' && !entry.disabled)"

    # DeepSeek account sign-in uses the Host-owned /oauth/callback route. A
    # TUI-only profile needs a loopback listener; a mixed Web+TUI profile
    # reuses Web's official webserver instead of opening a second one. Hosts
    # without an enabled account service row leave this listener disabled.
    - id: dsh-tui-webserver
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver'
      disabled: !!js >-
        (() => {
          const require = process.getBuiltinModule('node:module').createRequire(ctx.baseUrl)
          try { require.resolve('@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver/package.json') } catch { return true }
          const entries = [...ctx.loader.entries()]
          return !entries.some(entry => entry.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-deepseek-account-platform' && !entry.disabled)
            || entries.some(entry => entry.options.id === 'webserver' && entry.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver' && !entry.disabled)
        })()
      config:
        host: 127.0.0.1
        port: 0

    # Built-in subscription OAuth sign-in: mounts available pi-ai routes
    # (ChatGPT/Codex, Claude, Grok; newer pi-ai adds OpenAI direct and Meta)
    # plus the /auth command. Its facade also delegates DeepSeek sign-in to
    # the Host-owned account service when available. The TUI's /provider
    # wizard gains its OAuth branch from ctx.dshAuth. Entry-level inject only —
    # the internal module's own inject is empty so a stale patch cannot
    # deadlock a composition lacking these services (#183 pattern).
    - id: dsh-tui-auth
      name: '@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui/oauth'
      inject: [llm, commands]

    # The interactive front door. The plugin creates/resumes its agent at
    # runtime, seeds the startup status line, and disposes the whole app tree
    # (exiting the process) when the TUI unmounts. `dsh-tui --resume`
    # feeds the session id through DSH_TUI_RESUME_SESSION (see
    # src/sessionHistory.ts for the launcher contract).
    - id: dsh-tui
      name: '@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui'
      # The entry-level dependency augments the plugin's `agents` inject and
      # prevents startup Session creation from racing WorkspaceRegistry init.
      inject: [workspaceRegistry, agents, tuiWorkspaces, tuiScenes, tuiPanels, tuiDialogs, tuiStatus, tuiShortcuts, tuiRenderers, tuiThemes]
      # `tuiWorkspaces`/`tuiScenes` (and the dsh-tui-extensions services,
      # including `tuiThemes`)
      # live in the entry-level inject ONLY as an ordering (and reload-rebind)
      # guarantee alongside their service rows
      # above — they are deliberately absent from the plugin's code-level
      # inject (issue #183): the dsh CLI may read this patch from an older
      # copy of the package than the plugin module it loads, and a hard
      # code-level inject then deadlocks the tree at boot ("pending (waiting
      # for service: tuiWorkspaces)"). Without the rows the TUI degrades:
      # /workspace falls back to the local-only runtime, plugin scenes never
      # open. (The comment sits below the inject line:
      # verify-workspace-attachment.mjs asserts the name→inject distance.)
      config:
        # `provider` + `model` are the deployment DEFAULT route (used until a
        # `/model` pick is persisted in ~/.dsh-tui/model.json, which then wins
        # whole); a half-pinned pair is ignored outright (issue #67).
        provider: deepseek-official
        # Alt-screen fullscreen 布局：应用内鼠标选区（选择即复制, OSC 52 +
        # wl-copy/xclip/xsel 兜底）、滚轮滚动、双击选词/三击选行。出厂默认开启，
        # 与 schema 默认（index.ts fullscreen default true）保持一致——两处必须
        # 同步翻转，否则本覆盖层会盖住 schema 默认，更新后用户仍落在 inline。
        # 想退回 inline 主屏（终端原生滚动/选择）：/settings 全屏开关或 cordis.yml
        # `fullscreen: false`——显式选择始终优先于默认。
        fullscreen: true
        # 以下为 /settings 可改的显示设置；每项说明与默认值见应用内 /settings 屏。
        terminalImages: true
        # diffLayout: auto
        # mermaidDiagrams: true
        # 任务完成通知：off / unfocused（默认）/ always；方式：auto（默认）/ osc9 / bel / windows。
        # taskNotifications: unfocused
        # notificationMethod: auto
        # windows 档：Windows 主机原生 toast（首次注册当前用户的 HKCU 标识，约延迟 3 秒）。
        # auto 在 Windows 本地会话用此档，SSH 改走客户端终端；仅 DSH 会话且 cc-dsh-notifier 已启用、正在运行时让位。
        # 回复中 LaTeX 公式的显示方式：auto（默认，目前为 Unicode）/ image（支持图形的终端里块级公式显示为图片）/ unicode / source（保留源码）。/settings 可实时改。
        # mathRendering: auto
        # 每个请求实际生效的推理强度，按当前路由的 adapter 档位校验
        #（deepseek: off/low/high/max）；非法值回落 adapter 默认。
        # 这是部署默认值：上一次 /effort 的持久化选择（~/.dsh-tui/effort.json）
        # 优先于它，它只决定"还没有选择过"的会话。
        effort: max
        # Shift+Tab session-mode cycle (array order IS the cycle order;
        # absent → the built-in default/plan/full trio below). Each entry
        # may declare any subset of the plan (on/off), sandbox (read-only/
        # workspace-write/danger-full-access), and approval (ask/never)
        # atoms; undeclared atoms are untouched. Entry index 0 is the
        # unmarked base mode.
        # modes:
        #   - id: default
        #     plan: false
        #     sandbox: workspace-write
        #     approval: ask
        #   - id: plan
        #     plan: true
        #     sandbox: read-only
        #     approval: ask
        #   - id: full
        #     plan: false
        #     sandbox: danger-full-access
        #     approval: never
        # Deployment default for the Agent preset: the persisted `/preset`
        # preference (~/.dsh-tui/agent-preset.json) outranks it, and
        # DSH_TUI_PRESET (this run's explicit instruction) outranks both; the
        # roster default (standard) closes the chain.
        preset: !!js process.env.DSH_TUI_PRESET ?? undefined
        workspace: !!js process.env.DSH_TUI_WORKSPACE_TARGET ?? undefined
        sessionId: !!js process.env.DSH_TUI_RESUME_SESSION ?? undefined
        # Agent backend (`dsh-tui --backend claude` → DSH_TUI_BACKEND); unset → /kernel's remembered pick, else dsh.
        backend: !!js process.env.DSH_TUI_BACKEND || undefined

    # Live working-line data source (thinking copy / running tool / turn
    # summary). Mounted through @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui's own
    # `./working-activity` re-export, NOT the bare `dsh-working-activity`
    # name: the dsh Loader resolves row names from the profile directory,
    # and pnpm's isolated node_modules layout never links a transitive
    # dependency into the profile root (npm's flat layout hid this), so the
    # bare name died with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND and disposed the whole app at
    # boot (#60).
    # The plugin stays mounted for its narration/system-prompt features and
    # publishes the `workingActivity` session projection, which is where the

readme.text:
After startup the TUI checks for newer versions in the background. It never
blocks the first frame. Type `/update` for a one-shot upgrade of the whole set
— TUI, dsh engine and global launcher. It restarts automatically and resumes
the current session, and refuses instead of leaving an incompatible or
unbootable TUI/engine combination. Launcher alignment is normally best effort,
but a failure after the engine advances blocks the restart and prints a repair
command. If the registry has a newer dsh release outside the TUI's
validated line, it says so and waits for a TUI update rather than installing an
unvalidated engine. Launcher alignment only touches proven global installs;
local npm/npx packages, ambiguous aliases and multi-member pnpm groups stay
unchanged. See
[Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md) for the profile lifecycle,
source builds, and troubleshooting, including migration from the former
`dsh-cc-tui` package.

Automation: `dst -p "task"`, `dst run --json`, `dst session list --json`.
The independent engine does not load the TUI or inherit its profile/preferences;
it uses official DSH headless/services (validated on 0.2.0-rc.2, 0.2.1-rc.2, 0.2.1-rc.3, 0.2.1-rc.4 and 0.2.1-rc.5).
`dst cli --help` lists its commands; `dst dsh <argv...>` forwards native DSH.
See [Automation CLI](docs/cli.en.md) for protocol, limits, resume restrictions,
and Node/Python/PowerShell integration examples.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `dsh-tui` / `dst` | Start the TUI; `dst` is a short alias for the same program |
| `dsh-tui --resume [id]` · `dsh-tui update` · `dsh-tui doctor` | Resume a session · align the TUI, dsh engine and global launcher as one set · pre-flight environment checks |
| `dsh-tui safe` | Read-only diagnostics, plugin inventory and repair guidance; `safe --rescue` builds a clean rescue profile |
| `dsh-tui version` · `dsh-tui help` | Launcher and profile versions and usage; both work even without a `dsh` install |

Leading DSH options such as `--dump-config` and `--patch <path>` are forwarded
unchanged; other arguments go to the app in `dsh --profile dsh-tui`. Use
`dsh-tui -- --resume=sid-1 ./notes` to send `--resume=sid-1 ./notes` as literal
prompt text, without selecting a session or workspace. When invoking DSH
directly, use `dsh --profile dsh-tui -- -- --resume=sid-1 ./notes`: the first
`--` belongs to DSH, the second to the app. Host options can precede a literal
prompt: `dsh-tui --patch ./overlay.yml -- --resume=sid-1` applies the overlay
and sends `--resume=sid-1` as prompt text without resuming that session.

Bring Claude Code, Codex, OMP, zcode, or Grok Build conversation histories into the DSH session store, then browse and resume them by their original working directory via `/resume`:

```sh
dsh-tui migrate                # list importable counts per agent (writes nothing)
dsh-tui migrate claude-code    # import every Claude Code conversation (likewise codex / omp / zcode / grok-build)
dsh-tui migrate codex --dry-run  # preview what would land, write nothing
```

readme.section: Importing conversations from other agents (`dsh-tui migrate`)
readme.text:
- **Read-only source**: migration only reads the foreign agent's local store; artifacts are written through the official `JsonlSessionPersistence` backend, so imported sessions are first-class (openable, continuable).
- **Idempotent**: one deterministic UUID per source conversation — re-importing skips what is already present instead of stacking duplicates.
- **Structure preserved**: user/assistant messages, reasoning traces, tool calls with their results, and the source's context compactions (as native compaction checkpoints) are rebuilt turn by turn; harness-injected machine text opens no turn. An imported session can pick the work straight up.
In-TUI browsing: the session screen (`/resume`) shows a tab per agent that has conversations; picking one imports just that conversation and opens it.
In-TUI: `/migrate` (optionally `/migrate <agent> [--dry-run]`) runs the same import in a child process and reports through the notification flow.
CLI alternative: `dsh-tui migrate ...` from any shell runs the same import.
Full guide: [Session migration](docs/migrate.en.md).

Bare `--resume` (`-c`, `--continue`) reopens the last session of the backend this
launch selected. Startup recovery only ever targets that backend: a backend with no
last session, or a derived target that belongs to a different backend than the one
that actually booted (an unknown backend id falling back to DSH, `--backend` naming
a backend that is not installed, a remembered kernel that is not the marker's
source), refuses with a clear error and exit code 1 — never a silent cold start,
never another backend's session, never a new session. An explicit `--resume <id>`
passes that id to the selected backend as-is. The one exception is safe mode's
"retry normal startup": it retries the kernel and session recorded in
`last-run.json`, so a record whose backend is gone degrades to a warning plus a cold
start — that retry is the last way back.

Run your own Codex through `codex app-server`, sharing its configuration,
login, instructions, skills, hooks, MCP and native threads:

```sh
npm install -g @openai/codex@0.160.1
dsh-tui --backend codex
dsh-tui --backend codex --resume <thread-id>
```

Protocol baseline **0.160.1**, minimum **0.144.0**; other versions may show
drift. `CODEX_EXECUTABLE` selects a binary; `/kernel` remembers the backend.
`codex resume <id>` can open the same thread after the other writer exits.
This is not `migrate codex`, which imports history into DSH.
With native credentials, a writer conflict for an idle thread retained by the
official background server triggers a reconnection to that server. Managed
subscription credentials and `/channel` connections use private app-server processes.

Streaming/tool cards, approvals, questions, steer/queue/interrupt, model and
effort controls, Plan, `/review`, `/diff`, `/usage`, `/init`, skills and MCP
share the existing UI. Async questions open the questionnaire while Codex
continues working; answers steer the turn (or queue if unavailable), and
dismissing the question leaves work running. **Shift+Tab only toggles Plan**, keeping its underlying
permission preset; Full Access requires an explicit choice. Existing Codex
settings are respected, not overwritten with defaults. `/login` offers

credential store). Relay `/channel` connections take precedence; managed

shell did not export is injected from the DSH credential store when the ref
is stored there — the active store first, then the default `~/.dsh` one — so
keep the key in the store, no per-shell export needed. When nothing can
supply it, the session still starts and the reason is rep

For Claude and Codex, `/channel` tokens (`CHANNEL_*` refs) belong to the
active `DSH_HOME` only. Disconnecting a channel cannot revive a token from
the default home; reconnect it in the active home if needed. Provider
`env_key` credentials retain the fallback described above.

TPS includes hidden reasoning time and excludes tool execution time. Live
text estimates are corrected when Codex reports output token usage. Decode

DSH's experimental Agent Teams lets the session's agent (the Lead) create
named teammates that share the working directory, message each other and
coordinate on a shared task board. It ships with dsh, is off by default, and
`/plugin list` advertises it. Switch it on:

```sh
/plugin enable @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-profile
```

The switch enables or disables the bundle in the profile, so it persists
across restarts, and on a `dsh --profile` launch it applies at once — running
sessions included: the model is told which tools came and went. `/team` appears
in Help and `/` completion only once the team service is mounted, and only
reports: `/team` (or `/team status`) shows the bundle, the service and this
session's teammates. `/team on|off` was removed; typing it points at
`/plugin enable|disable`. Turning the bundle off while teammates run asks
first, and switching off stops them: the team service releases the teammates
still running as it unloads. Inside a teammate session the other teammates'
runs are not visible, so the question counts them as possibly running. The
team record stays in the session and comes back when the bundle is enabled
again.

If the running DSH does not ship the bundle (`/plugin list` stays silent),
switch DSH to one of the supported lines first (`0.2.2-rc.1`, `0.2.1-rc.5`, `0.2.1-rc.4`, `0.2.1-rc.3`,
`0.2.1-rc.2`, `0.2.1-alpha.5`, `0.2.0-rc.1` or `0.2.0-rc.2`). To install it into the profile explicitly,
run `dsh plugin --profile dsh-tui add @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-profile@<your-dsh-version>`:
the team packages ship in lockstep with DSH and pin their DSH peers exactly,
so the version must match.

While a request carries `spawn_teammate`, dsh-TUI drops `subagent` /
`subagent_fork` from it, and the team's `send_message` / `list_agents` /
`interrupt_agent` / `wait_agent` take the place of the legacy controls of the
same names, so `spawn_teammate` is the delegation tool; with the team off
the legacy tools are back. Subagents that are not team members (workflow,
ralph) keep `subagent`. A teammate shows up as a subagent row, a message between
members as a `✉ <sender>` bubble in the receiving session (a teammate's
received messages show on its subagent detail as agent messages), and the
other team tools as one-line cards (`send_message` with its target and
`sent`). The agents dashboard (Ctrl+A) and the agents side
panel switch to a team view: each teammate under its member name with
`running` / `idle` / `provisioning` / `failed` (a teammate whose turn ended
is idle — a message wakes it — not done), the Lead line, the remaining
subagents, a read-only task board (status, owner, `blocked`, write-scope
warnings) and a banner when the team record was rejected. A delegation
provider whose settled runs fail at least twice and at least half the time
gets one degraded-channel line above th

Limits: the switch covers the whole profile, not one session (a launch
without the profile plugin service, or without hot reload, needs `dsh plugin`
and a restart); there is no "enter teammate session" yet, and `/export` leaves team messages out. Upstream limits apply: teammates share one working directory, a
team lives in one process, and a task owner is never released automatically.
Subagent failure badges and the Companion error state share session-scoped unread
status. Opening that child’s detail or main view acknowledges only that failure;
a new run or failure alerts again. Acknowledgements survive panel remounts and
session switches during this process, but a cold restart starts unread. Opening
the dashboard alone does not acknowledge every child. Task status stays failed.

`Enter` send · `Tab` complete · `Ctrl+Enter` interrupt and send · `Alt+Up` recall the last message · `Esc` closes local layers before interrupting a running turn, double-`Esc` rewinds on empty idle input · `Ctrl+B` side panel · `Ctrl+O` details · `Ctrl+R` history (`↑`/`↓` and `Ctrl+R` are scoped to the current project) · `Ctrl+V` paste · `Ctrl+Shift+E` fullscreen draft editor · `?` shortcuts · `←` open the session manager (DSH backgrounds the current session first).
In both the launchpad and chat, `Ctrl+U` deletes from the caret to the current line start, preserving text to the right and whole image chips. It edits only the focused input.

In the launchpad input, `Shift+Enter` (or `Option+Enter`) opens chat and inserts a newline at the caret, keeping the draft and staged images unsent. Continue typing there, then press `Enter` to send.

In both the launchpad and chat, `Alt/Option+←/→` moves by whitespace-delimited words and `Alt/Option+Backspace` deletes the previous word, like `Ctrl+W`. On macOS, configure your terminal to send Option as Meta.

Use `Alt+Up` / `Alt+Down` to page through question text and details, or approval previews on very short terminals, without moving the choice focus; these keys are remappable in `/settings` → `Shortcuts`. Fullscreen also supports the wheel over the preview. Complete OAuth links remain readable when browser and clipboard helpers are unavailable. Fixed-action permission questions offer only the caller's choices; ordinary questionnaires still accept free text.

Text, cursor position and staged image attachments on the launchpad or in chat while the backend starts are preserved when the session becomes ready. Press `Enter` after it is ready to send; an earlier `Enter` preserves the draft without queuing it. Opening a new session while startup is pending clears the previous draft and its images.

The goal bar stays on one summary line: hovering truncated goal text in fullscreen or split shows the whole objective, and a bare `/goal` prints the full status — objective, phase, rounds or budget, available commands — as a transcript block in the `/plugins` shape. Inline mode sees no pointer events, so that block is how its users read a long objective.

While the model is working: `Enter` steers, `Tab` queues a follow-up, `Ctrl+Enter` interrupts and sends. Input that names a command is still a command — with or without arguments — so `/model` or `/new` reach their own gate (and the `/` overlay sinks the commands that affect the running conversation) instead of silently becoming an interruption; only text that is not a command — and a direct skill gesture such as `/skill-name …` — steers.

When DSH ends a turn because its session was disposed, the transcript shows “Session stopped”; user interruption keeps its existing prompt for what to do next. This describes the reported stop reason and does not recover a stuck session or its queued inputs.

Windows Neovim/Vim terminals identified by `NVIM` or `VIM_TERMINAL` retain VT input instead of enabling ConPTY mode 9001. For another incompatible embedded host, set `DSH_TUI_DISABLE_WIN32_INPUT_MODE=1` before launch (PowerShell: `$env:DSH_TUI_DISABLE_WIN32_INPUT_MODE="1"`). The same gate applies at startup and after resume. Native Windows Terminal, conhost and VS Code keep their existing mode unless disabled; the opt-out can remove modified-Enter reporting.

Extended key reporting (Kitty keyboard protocol and xterm `modifyOtherKeys`) is enabled for a fixed terminal list: iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm, Ghostty, rio, Orca, tmux, Warp and Windows Terminal. A terminal missing from that list can opt in with `DSH_TUI_FORCE_EXTENDED_KEYS=1`, and `DSH_TUI_DISABLE_EXTENDED_KEYS=1` opts an allowlisted terminal back out for SSH or nested xterm.js hosts (it wins when both are set). Outside native Windows, where win32-input-mode reports Enter's modifiers instead and is not touched by this switch, a terminal without extended keys cannot tell `Shift+Enter` from `Enter`, and `Ctrl+J` is the newline fallback.

On native Windows, fragmented Win32 input records are reassembled across short input delays instead of appearing as numeric protocol text. The platform check only reports that this machine might run the private mode (win32-input-mode); a bare `ESC[` fragment is held only after one record has actually been decoded, while a fragment whose own shape is already record-specific holds on its own (which is how even the first record can survive a split). Windows terminals that never enter the mode (mintty, GitBash) therefore keep the classic VT path: a lone `Esc` keeps its normal response time, and a letter typed after a timed-out `ESC[` is not swallowed.

Incomplete records are held for a bounded recovery window (1 second from first capture, never extended by later input; 64 bytes max); past either bound the hold ends and input is handled as before. Unrecognized complete CSI sequences are not inserted as text; after a damaged CSI prefix, a bare ASCII letter can be consumed as its terminator, while normal Win32 key records and bracketed-paste text retain their own boundaries.

A session's very first record can still leave residue if it is split before its record-specific shape forms; once any record has been decoded, every split position is covered. Inside the recovery window, literal input starting with `[digit;…` cannot be told apart from a protocol prefix — it may be held, or re-joined to a preceding `Esc`. To type it, wait for the window to close, or avoid that shape right after `Esc`.

Terminal replies that arrive split are reassembled the same way (native Windows ConPTY is the common source): while the app still has a query awaiting its answer, an unfinished DA1 / DA2 / DSR / DECRPM / XTVERSION tail — even one split again after the introducer `Esc` was flushed — is held across input delays, but only while its shape can still complete into the response type that query expects. It is then consumed as the reply it completes instead of entering the prompt as protocol text.

That claim is evidence-gated, and this is the difference from earlier builds: no query awaiting an answer means nothing is claimed, so a literal `[?61;4c` typed right after `Esc` still enters the prompt exactly as before.

The window is bounded like the record hold (about a second, never extended by later input; 64 bytes max); past either bound it ends, and bytes still shaped like an unfinished reply prefix are dropped rather than shown.

Inside that window, with a query of the matching response type outstanding, same-shaped literal input can still be claimed as a reply; to type it, wait for the window to close (about a second), or avoid that shape while a query is outstanding.

Fragmented SGR mouse reports no longer land in the prompt as text: an incomplete report header is held until the rest arrives, and a report that completes is handled as a mouse event. The hold is armed only while mouse reporting is actually active (fullscreen, with mouse tracking enabled); inline sessions and terminals that never enable tracking keep the existing behavior. The claim window is bounded from first capture (at most 1 second; 64 bytes max), and a continuation arriving inside it is still claimed rather than replayed. Release has no timer: once a parse call sees either bound exceeded, it replays the held bytes as ordinary keys in arrival order — literal input can be delayed, but is never dropped.
A completed text-only assistant reply containing only a leading `⏵` status line remains visible in the conversation and can be selected for copying. Live status lines and status lines followed by a real answer stay out of the transcript body.

Plugin slash-command results, including errors, remain as local transcript blocks for scrolling and copying during the current session. Indentation and line breaks are preserved. Each report retains at most 200 lines, 65,536 UTF-16 code units and 4,000 terminal cells per line, plus a visible truncation marker. The local display rows are not sent as model input or replayed as conversation history. The backend may separately persist command audit events and their results. Older local report blocks are evicted within the shared 600-row budget. Explicit built-in report layouts (such as `/goal`) keep their existing formatting.

When a fullscreen selection starts in a code block's body, soft-wrapped rows join without adding frame padding or newlines, in both light and full frames. Hard line breaks and the existing hard-line inset remain part of screen copying.

During a fullscreen text drag, the native cursor follows the selected text's edge using your terminal's enabled cursor animation or trail effects. Moving into trailing padding or blank rows keeps it at the nearest selected text edge. Releasing or cancelling the drag restores the focused input's caret.
File paths in prose can open the file-action menu; automatic detection does not extract a path from inside a slash-delimited token such as `working/idle/needs-input` or a date such as `2024/01/15`.

**Pasting**: the launchpad accepts clipboard images and pasted image paths as `[Image #N]` attachments; `Enter` sends them with the first message. Commands that do not accept images preserve the draft and its attachments. Image chips behave like chat: arrows step across them, Backspace at the end or Delete at the start removes the whole image, and Ctrl+W never splits a chip. Text pasted on the launchpad is folded to one line. In chat, native and bracketed paste keeps ordinary text and newlines, and never submits itself on arrival. On Windows terminals that deliver a paste as win32-input-mode key records, a record stream leaked into the payload is decoded back into the characters its `Uc` field encodes — newlines included — so the composer's line count matches what was pasted; only records with no character meaning are stripped (a multi-line paste no longer leaves stray `_`), and a complete record is always consumed before an ESC-less tail, so no payload character is deleted along with an orphan escape. Pasted CRLF collapses to a single newline; genuine underscores and bracketed-paste text are untouched.

Image paths enter the existing image staging pipeline; other files are inserted as a referenceable path (a path containing whitespace arrives in the composer's quoted `"…"` single-token form). Only `file://` URIs are restored, and it is fail-closed: a remote authority/UNC, a payload carrying several distinct URIs, or a URI that carries several tokens is refused and stays literal text rather than guessed.

A spec names one of three things:

```sh
/plugin install /path/to/repo
/plugin install https://github.com/exam/ple.git
/plugin install @scope/package@1.2.3
```

Typing `/plugin install ` lists these three shapes in the completion popup, and the same shapes follow the installed names on `/plugin info `. They are examples, never candidates: `Tab` leaves the draft exactly as it is, and `Enter` runs the line you typed — the subcommand's usage line while the spec is still empty, your own spec once it is not. No example can therefore be inserted or installed by accident, and a real path that merely starts like one is never swallowed.

During installation, `esc` attempts cancellation and keeps the pane open until the write settles; if cancellation is too late, it waits for the installation to finish. During exemption registration, it waits for the current write and stops subsequent grants and the retry. Exemptions already written remain.

Failed installs show up to six redacted log lines; lines larger than 16 KiB are omitted with a notice.

Managing what is installed: `/plugin remove <bundle>`, `/plugin enable <name | row id>` and `/plugin disable <name | row id>`. A bundle is a composition layer and a row is one patch entry, so the two are separate actions, and a bundle name is matched before any row identity. A module name shared by multiple rows requires a specific row ID. **Gate 2 refuses the three ways this app could switch itself off** — removing or disabling the bundle that provides it, the host layer `dsh-base`, or one of its own rows — and says which rule it broke, without calling the service at all; that holds whether or not hot reload is live, which is the path the host's own guard misses. `enable` is never refused by gate 2 (it is the repair action). Every enable and removal asks first; `disable` asks only about a host-layer row. The host does not attest installed package sources, so even an exact feed match requires confirmation before enabling.

These three actions have no cancellation — the service offers none — so `esc` only closes the pane while the write finishes and reports itself into the transcript. Enable and disable have no CLI verb either (the service writes them into the profile's own files). **Grants follow the lifecycle**: `enable` enables and grants the declared permissions, `disable` disables and revokes the permissions that component declared, and `remove` **deletes the component's `grants`/`denies` entries** after the removal — grants are keyed by component id, so leaving them behind lets any later package reusing that id inherit them silently; a reinstall asks again. Backend data directories, storage namespaces and the effect ledger stay, and the residue report names each source by its path. A failed grant write never blocks an install or enable — it is reported instead. Grants are behavioural constraints, not a security boundary.

No sandbox of its own: dsh-TUI uses the active DSH profile's filesystem, shell, sandbox and approval policies. Permission presets come from the DSH `permissionPresets` registry.

**Permission persistence** (all three backends): the Claude and Codex backends keep their `/permission` picks in `~/.dsh-tui/backends/<id>/prefs.json`; the DSH pick is kept at `~/.dsh-tui/permission.json`. Every durable preset switch teaches it (picker, typed `/permission`, Shift+Tab static modes, or a switch the official command performed on its own), and a session that never customized its permission planes starts on the remembered preset — applied through the same official switch path. "Never customized" is about the user: the composition writes its own default preset into every fresh session at creation, and those events do not count. Plan-mode transients and the experimental Auto review preset (see below) are excluded, a `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE` launch pin (this run's initial permission plane) outranks the file, and an identity the mounted roster no longer offers is skipped.

It is session-only: the model reviews every tool call before it runs, there is no file sandbox, and each call costs one extra model request; its approval prompts show the localized reason, and a subagent denial reads "Auto review denied; not executed". Picking it in the picker first shows a risk confirmation (`Enter` enables, `Esc` goes back; in fullscreen its Enable / Go back rows are clickable); a typed `/permission auto` switches directly. Once the current session has selected it, the picker skips the confirmation and Shift+Tab stops skipping it.

The index is in memory and is built on the first search; nothing is written to disk. This app keeps the kernel Minimal preset at its single persistent-shell tool, so Minimal never shows these five tools or their usage guidance.

`/update` and `dsh-tui update` give each installer invocation (profile and engine) a **30-minute
wall-clock limit**. Set `DSH_TUI_UPDATE_TIMEOUT_MS` to a positive integer in
milliseconds to change it (invalid values use the default). Output activity does
not reset this deadline; a quiet but healthy installation can use the full limit.
Only the final process exit code establishes success: a printed `Done` does not.
Ctrl+C cancels the owned installer. On POSIX, cancellation terminates its own
process group, then force-kills remaining descendants after two seconds. Windows
uses a dedicated PowerShell/native supervisor with a private Job Object. The
installer joins that job atomically while suspended; verified membership is required
before it runs. The supervisor retains the job handle after the root exits, so
cancellation and timeout also terminate orphaned descendants holding output pipes.
It does not enable job breakaway or kill processes by name or an exited root PID.

Windows requires Windows 10 / Server 2016 or later and Windows PowerShell with
`Add-Type`/native interop available. Startup or job-membership failures stop the
installation before running an unowned installer. A cleanup failure is reported as
unconfirmed, never as proof that all writes stopped. Timeout, cancellation, or
unconfirmed cleanup returns nonzero and prevents retries, stale-file removal,
repair, and TUI replacement. A partial installation may remain: check/repair that
profile before using the recovery command printed at update start and on failure.
`~/.dsh-tui/restart.log` records installer category, PID, termination reason and last
output timestamp before any restart.

The focused **Windows installer process ownership** workflow runs the real native
regression on `windows-latest`, with Node 24 and no dependency installation. To run
it locally on Windows: `node scripts/verify-update-process-windows.mjs`. It checks
orphan descendants, timeout/cancellation, nested jobs, failure diagnostics, streams,
arguments and an unrelated process; a Linux run explicitly skips native acceptance.
